My Memory
My Memory · Pocket Knowledge

Snap anything, it remembers.
Ask anything, it finds it.

My Memory is a second memory that lives in your pocket — like human memory, except it never makes things up. Snap a photo, dictate a voice memo, jot a quick note: everything is written into one shared memory, right on your device. When you need it, just ask — it hands back the original capture as proof.

The three core screens

Remembers like a human.
But only tells the truth.

Human memory “recalls” things wrong. My Memory is not allowed to: every number and every detail must come from the original capture — and when there is no evidence, it says so plainly.

The feature that makes the difference

A good memory is a memory that knows how to forget.

Capture everything and clutter will get in — everyone knows that. My Memory's difference: it actively tidies its own memory, under one iron rule — suggesting is allowed, deleting on its own is never allowed. Try approving the queue below:

The forgetting rules — hard-coded, non-negotiable

Deleting the wrong photo loses it forever. Keeping an extra one costs a few MB. So every rule leans towards keeping.

Suggest only — never auto-delete

Every act of forgetting starts as a suggestion with evidence. Without your nod, nothing disappears.

Reasons must be verifiable

“0.97 duplicate”, “expired on 10 Nov”, “a newer version was captured later” — concrete numbers, one tap to see the original capture. A vague “not relevant” is never enough to suggest.

30-day trash, always restorable

Even after you approve, nothing is gone yet: 30 days in the trash, restorable at any time. Forgetting must have a way back.

What you keep teaches it

Every time you keep an item it suggested deleting, that choice teaches My Memory your taste, so the next suggestions are less wrong. The human always has the final say.

How it runs

Local first. Cloud later — and only when needed.

Your voice and daily habits are the most private data you have. So most of My Memory runs right on the phone; the cloud only joins when you need a long, synthesised answer.

1

Save — 3 ways in, 1 memory

Photos, voice memos and text notes are all transcribed and embedded with EmbeddingGemma on-device, into the same vector space. That is why a text question can find a photo.

2

Ask — local search, cited answers

Search runs offline, under 1 second for a personal capture store. Answers always attach the original capture; no citation, no answer — better to say “not found” than to make something up.

3

Forget — suggest, approve, then delete

Periodically, My Memory scans for duplicates and expired items and queues them with evidence. You approve each item; deleted items spend 30 days in the trash before they are truly gone.

01

Never fabricates

Human memory fills gaps with imagined detail. My Memory does the opposite: every number must come from the original capture, verifiable in one tap.

02

Never deletes on its own

The AI suggests, the human decides. This is a hard product boundary — there is no “smart auto-clean” mode that can be quietly switched on.

03

No network required

Pull the SIM, turn on airplane mode, lose signal in a lift — your memory is still there and still answers. Because it never left your device.

Hybrid architecture · Firebase AI Logic

The same three screens, wired the hybrid way.

My Memory calls the Firebase AI Logic SDK at runtime and lets it choose, per request, between on-device and cloud. The rule never changes: originals stay on the phone, only light summaries ever travel.

Screen 1 · On-device ingestion

Capture → Gemini Nano, PREFER_ON_DEVICE

When you photograph a receipt or a medicine box, Firebase AI Logic runs in PREFER_ON_DEVICE mode with Gemini Nano 4. The image never leaves the phone, costs nothing to process, and comes back as one flat structured JSON record — the exact fields the forgetting rules will later read.

{ "summary": "Lunch receipt 256,000₫", "entities": ["total", "date", "place"], "expiryDate": "2027-03" }
  • Photos & text notes — Nano takes text and text+image, and returns summary, entities and expiryDate.
  • Voice memos do NOT go through Nano. They are transcribed by a separate on-device ASR (or embedded directly as audio with EmbeddingGemma); only the resulting text can be handed to Nano.
  • Flat schema, on purpose — on-device structured output is still young, so the JSON stays shallow and predictable.
Screen 2 · Hybrid retrieval

Local answer first, cloud only for deep synthesis

A normal question is answered entirely on the device. Only a question that must reason across many captures and many months escalates — and even then, what travels is the light JSON summaries, never the original photos or audio.

  • Local path (< 1s, offline) — search the on-device vector store (IndexedDB / local vectors), then Gemini Nano drafts a short, cited answer. Airplane mode changes nothing.
  • Cloud escalation — “Total up this month's lunches, and check whether mum's current medicine interacts with the new prescription photographed yesterday” goes to cloud Gemini (Flash / Pro) via Firebase AI Logic.
  • Originals stay home — the cloud receives summaries and entities only; every claim in its answer must still cite a capture that lives on the device.
Screen 3 · Forget Lab

Local rules + hybrid scoring, human approves

The forget queue is built on the device from two signals that already exist locally: how similar two captures are, and the expiryDate Nano extracted at capture time. Nothing about forgetting needs the cloud — and nothing is deleted without approval.

  • Cosine similarity, locally — a new photo scoring 0.97 against one taken 40 seconds earlier is queued as a duplicate, with the score shown as evidence.
  • Expiry from ingestion — an expiryDate in the past (an OTP, a medicine date) queues the capture as expired.
  • Thresholds are tunable — Firebase Remote Config sets the suggestion threshold (for example 0.95 or 0.97), so the strictness can change without an app update. The approval rule itself is never a config value.
RequiredFirebase App Check

App Check is switched on for the Firebase AI Logic calls, so only the real app — not a copied key in a script — can reach the models.

Firestore, offline persistence on

Firestore with offline persistence syncs metadata only — summaries, entities, expiry dates — between phone and computer. The original photos and audio never sync; they stay on the device that captured them.

Firebase Remote Config

Remote Config carries the tunable knobs — above all the duplicate threshold for forget suggestions (0.95 / 0.97) — so behaviour can be tuned without shipping a new build.
